note:
Lenton Road on the 1901 census - the households the record and the existing import files did not already hold.

**Nine whole households are new**: Harpenden, Cleveden, Ravine House, 23 Lenton Road, Leslie House, Yeldersley House, Villa Vanely, Weston Lodge, and the household of Louisa H. Williams, a widow of 65 with six grown children among them two lace manufacturers and a cigar merchant.

**They are unfiled unless the page gives a number**, because the record keeps this street by number and the enumerator kept it by name - Harpenden, Cleveden, Ravine House, Leslie House, Rock House, Yeldersley House, Villa Vanely, Weston Lodge, Fern Lodge, Cliff House, Lenton House. Only a few carry numbers.

**Eight houses here are already filed by other files** - 9, 13, 15, 17, 25 and 29 Lenton Road, Cliff House and Rock House - and nothing in this file touches them.

**Anyone already written into another 1901 file is left out of this one.** Most of these households are part done - the existing files hold the head and some of the servants but not the children, or the other way about - so the skipping is person by person rather than household by household, and what remains is only what no committed file already carries.

**Some people were taken out of this file after it was first written.** They already had a 1901 census row in another file in data/ - in one case a whole household, the Dobsons of 23 Lenton Road, recorded there under fuller names and filed to the house. Keeping them here would have described the same census night twice.
source: 1901 census enumerator's page for Lenton Road, Nottingham, transcribed by A. Hagues.
